boundary_rationale: The unit opens where the scene turns from darkened lands into light, at כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ (oshb:Isa.8.23, byte tier), rendered “But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.” (web:Isa.9.1) = oshb:Isa.8.23; the causal particle opening that verse recurs verse-initially inside the span at oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6), so the seam rests on the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle. A fresh nominal subject then opens the following verse, הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ (oshb:Isa.9.1, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.2, and the address turns second person at הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי (oshb:Isa.9.2, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.3, continued by הַחִתֹּ֖תָ (oshb:Isa.9.3, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.4; the unit is read as one sustained declaration, not because no fresh subject or addressee arises — both do — but because the chain of causal ki-clauses that follows (כִּ֣י אֶת עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ, oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4; כִּ֤י כָל סְאוֹן֙, oshb:Isa.9.4 = web:Isa.9.5) restates the same reason as the opening light and the multiplied joy, before the birth clause returns to third person, כִּי יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד (oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.6, without a further break in the argument. The throne-naming clause reads פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִי עַ֖ד שַׂר שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier), rendered “His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (web:Isa.9.6 = oshb:Isa.9.5); an OSHB exegesis note sits at this same verse (oshb:Isa.9.5), single-witness apparatus only, never text bytes, and is disclosed rather than argued as content. The unit closes at the government-increase clause, which the letter bytes stage as a doubled ketiv/qere token pair לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה (oshb:Isa.9.6, byte tier) — the ketiv form carries a final mem in medial position; the quote engages both staged forms, not one alone — rendered “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6). No addressee or subject marker reopens before web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence, so the throne clause stays inside this unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the light-dawning announcement from the throne-naming and its government clause is rejected because the chain of coordinated ki-clauses keeps both halves inside one argument for the nation's joy.

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah break follows oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7), tier-3 single-witness corroboration only, for a close already argued from the ki-chain and the fresh subject at web:Isa.9.8; it is never treated as the driver. A ketiv/qere note also sits at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3), inside this unit's own span; it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here without a content claim resting on either reading. The medial final-mem in the doubled token is letter bytes plus ketiv/qere apparatus, not a special-letter seg of any size. The referent of the throne names (a court style exalting a Davidic king, versus a fuller messianic reading) is not settled by this boundary decision and is held open.

boundary_rationale: A fresh declarative sentence with a new grammatical subject opens the unit: דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְנָפַ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.9.7, byte tier), “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.” (web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7); Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria stand in apposition to the subject of the third-person plural verb that follows, וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.9.8, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.9 — an appositional expansion of that subject, not an addressed object — and the shift from the preceding unit's royal house is a shift of the oracle's target rather than of addressee: no second-person verb or suffix appears at any verse from oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) through oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12). The unit closes at the refrain bracket אֲרָ֣ם מִקֶּ֗דֶם וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ מֵֽאָח֔וֹר וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּכָל פֶּ֑ה בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.11, byte tier), “For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.12 = oshb:Isa.9.11).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this stanza through the next refrain occurrence is rejected because the following material renews the indictment with fresh content rather than continuing the same clause. A larger rival reads the whole judgment sequence as one continuous poem opening already at web:Isa.5.25 (the refrain recurs across five verses; sweep: 5 verses), with this stanza as a later movement rather than a fresh onset.

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark follows oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7), the verse immediately preceding this unit; tier-3, single-witness, disclosed even though the boundary is argued from the subject change rather than the mark. The closing refrain recurs byte-identically at five sites across the book (sweep: 5 verses), earliest at web:Isa.5.25, and on that basis a rival architecture reads the whole run from there as one continuous poem rather than granting this stanza its own bracket — disclosed rather than adopted.

boundary_rationale: A verse-initial nominal subject resumes the same referent already carrying the preceding stanza: וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא שָׁ֖ב (oshb:Isa.9.12, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.13 takes up הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.8, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.9, both at byte tier; the unit continues the same indictment before closing at its own refrain occurrence, עַל כֵּ֨ן עַל בַּחוּרָ֜יו לֹֽא יִשְׂמַ֣ח אֲדֹנָ֗י וְאֶת יְתֹמָ֤יו וְאֶת אַלְמְנֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔ם כִּ֤י כֻלּוֹ֙ חָנֵ֣ף וּמֵרַ֔ע וְכָל פֶּ֖ה דֹּבֵ֣ר נְבָלָ֑ה בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.16, byte tier), “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.17 = oshb:Isa.9.16).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this stanza as the poem's opening unit is rejected because its own onset resumes the same referent carrying the preceding judgment rather than introducing a fresh one. The same refrain closes web:Isa.5.25 as well as the other stanza-ends in this run (sweep: 5 verses), so a rival reading folds every stanza back into one long poem beginning there instead of granting this one a separate boundary.

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark is keyed at oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13), this unit's own opening verse; tier-3, single-witness, and the mark falls immediately after that verse, grouping it with the material preceding rather than opening a new paragraph there — so as corroboration it bears against this front seam rather than for it, disclosed rather than treated as a driver. boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a fresh image continuing the same judgment voice, “For wickedness burns like a fire.” (web:Isa.9.18 = oshb:Isa.9.17), and closes at its own refrain occurrence: בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.20, byte tier), “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.21 = oshb:Isa.9.20).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this stanza into the woe-oracle that follows is rejected because the addressee shifts from the punished nation to a class of officials identified by participial description rather than by name, after the refrain closes here, not before. The refrain's five occurrences (sweep: 5 verses) start at web:Isa.5.25 and support a rival view that the entire sequence is one interrupted poem rather than four bracketed stanzas.

Because the same byte-level refrain also closes web:Isa.5.25 and its other three sites (sweep: 5 verses), a rival architecture folds this stanza into one long poem beginning there rather than granting it an independent boundary — disclosed rather than adopted.

boundary_rationale: A new woe-onset addresses a wholly different subject — Assyria, not the decree-writers of the preceding unit: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט (oshb:Isa.10.5, byte tier), “Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!” (web:Isa.10.5). The unit runs through Assyria's own boastful self-assessment and closes at the rhetorical question comparing Jerusalem to Samaria, הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי (oshb:Isa.10.11, byte tier), “shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?” (web:Isa.10.11), before a fresh temporal-response clause opens the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through the king's boast quotation that follows is rejected because a temporal-response clause opens a distinct divine reply rather than continuing Assyria's own self-description.
literature_type_guess: woe oracle against Assyria as unwitting instrument

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.10.4 and another closes this one at web:Isa.10.11; both tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the boundary is argued from the addressee shift and the response clause that follows, not from the marks. The quotation formula כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר (oshb:Isa.10.8, byte tier), “Aren’t all of my princes kings?” (web:Isa.10.8), separates the divine first-person speech of web:Isa.10.5-web:Isa.10.7 from the king's own quoted boast running web:Isa.10.8-web:Isa.10.11; the unit is held together across that internal frame because the boast is itself the content the divine word introduces, addressed to the same Assyrian figure in both halves, so the quotation is read as continuing the speech rather than opening a fresh unit. A ketiv/qere note also sits at web:Isa.10.6, staged as the doubled pair ולשימו וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ (oshb:Isa.10.6, byte tier); it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here without a content claim resting on either reading, matching the practice this part already follows elsewhere.

boundary_rationale: A temporal-response formula opens the divine reply to Assyria's arrogance: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי יְבַצַּ֤ע (oshb:Isa.10.12, byte tier), “Therefore it will happen that when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his arrogant looks.” (web:Isa.10.12). A further therefore-clause לָ֠כֵן (oshb:Isa.10.16, byte tier) restates the same sentence rather than opening a new addressee, and the unit closes with the forest stripped bare, “The remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child could write their number.” (web:Isa.10.19).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the two therefore-clauses at web:Isa.10.12 and web:Isa.10.16 as separate rows is rejected because the king's own quoted boast, opened by the quotation frame at oshb:Isa.10.13, sits between them, and the unity is argued over that quotation rather than over any shared addressee, since neither therefore-clause has one.
literature_type_guess: judgment speech answering the instrument's boast

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.10.11 and a petuchah mark closes this one at web:Isa.10.19; both tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the internal therefore-clause at web:Isa.10.16 is treated as continuing the same speech rather than as a further seam, since no addressee change accompanies it. The forest imagery that closes this unit carries the remnant noun וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.10.19, byte tier); here it functions as a plain common noun, a different object from the name-reactivating clauses argued in the unit that follows. A ketiv/qere note also sits at web:Isa.10.13, staged as the doubled pair ועתידתיהם וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.10.13, byte tier); it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here for consistency with this part's own practice elsewhere, without a content claim resting on either reading.

boundary_rationale: A formulaic 'in that day' onset opens the unit with the remnant of Israel as its subject: וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.10.20, byte tier), “It will come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and those who have escaped from the house of Jacob will no more again lean on him who struck them, but shall lean on Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.” (web:Isa.10.20). The reactivating clause שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב שְׁאָ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֶל אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.10.21, byte tier) restates the son's sign-name given at web:Isa.7.3, “A remnant will return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.” (web:Isa.10.21); the unit closes with the severity coda, “For the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will make a full end, and that determined, throughout all the earth.” (web:Isa.10.23), before a distinct divine-word formula opens the following unit, כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier), “the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, says,” (web:Isa.10.24).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading only the return of the remnant (web:Isa.10.20-web:Isa.10.21) as the bounded unit is rejected because the full-end clause that follows shares the same 'in that day' frame and the same remnant vocabulary rather than opening independently.
literature_type_guess: remnant-return oracle with a judgment coda

device_notes: This unit engages the remnant root through three roles carried by one adjacency: the son's name at וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier), the name-reactivating clause opening שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב (oshb:Isa.10.21, byte tier), and the plain clause opening שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב (oshb:Isa.10.22, byte tier); the adjacency reaches 3 verses at skeleton tier, and at byte tier the accented run is shared by web:Isa.7.3 and web:Isa.10.22 alone (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier), web:Isa.10.21 differing from the other two in its accents. The plain common noun שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Isa.10.20, byte tier) is reserved for its own bare construct, which carries no adjacent return-verb; the separate collective-remnant noun and the survive-verb family remain different objects not engaged here. The signature divine title יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.10.20, byte tier) stands in this unit's own onset verse. A petuchah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.10.19 and a setumah mark closes this one at web:Isa.10.23; both tier-3, single-witness.

boundary_rationale: A divine messenger formula opens the unit: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier), “Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, says,” (web:Isa.10.24), addressed directly to Zion rather than continuing the third-person remnant announcement of the preceding unit. The unit closes with the promised relief, “It will happen in that day that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil.” (web:Isa.10.27), before the scene shifts to the march narrative that follows (web:Isa.10.28).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the assurance oracle through the march description that follows is rejected because that description opens with a fresh narrative scene rather than continuing the same divine-word formula.
literature_type_guess: messenger-formula oracle of assurance to Zion

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.10.23; tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the boundary is argued from the fresh koh-amar frame rather than the mark. This koh-amar is counted in the divine-frame class, not the royal-messenger class used elsewhere in the book's narrative material. The divine title stack opening this unit, אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier), is byte-identical to the stack closing the immediately preceding verse, אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.23, byte tier) — the book's only byte-tier occurrence of the stack (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier, 8 verses at skeleton tier) — and the seam still stands across it because the preceding verse carries the stack as the subject of a third-person judgment clause, while this verse's identical stack is the subject of the messenger verb אָמַ֞ר (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier) introducing a fresh, directly addressed assurance to Zion, so the recurrence alone does not carry the argument across the seam. This unit's own closing verse likewise opens with the in-that-day formula וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.10.27, byte tier), byte-identical to the formula that opens web:Isa.10.20, וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.10.20, byte tier), where it functions as a unit-opening driver (sweep: 5 verses at byte tier, 13 verses at skeleton tier); here the same formula stands unremarked inside the unit rather than opening it, so its boundary force is disclosed symmetrically rather than asserted selectively.
